newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech crown pressured after deputy PM resignation.
newsitem.headline: Czech crown pressured after deputy PM resignation.

text.p: The Czech crown slipped on Wednesday morning against its mark/dollar basket following the resignation on Tuesday evening of Deputy Prime Minister Jan Kalvoda.
"The reason (for the fall) is very clear. It is the problem with Kalvoda," said Tomas Becvar of Komercni Banka.

At 1028 GMT (1128 local time) the crown was trading at 2.27 percent above the mid-point of its mark/dollar basket from 2.45 percent just after the open. The dollar was at 27.466 while the mark was at 17.701.
Becvar said there had been strong selling pressure from London based institutions.
"The biggest investment banks are very active...there is strong pressure for selling the Czech crown," he said.
Support was seen at around 2.2 percent above the mid-point of the mark/dollar basket. Becvar said he expected the crown to hold above this point which he described as "very important."
The resignation of the deputy prime minister, who is also the Justice Minister, came after he admitted that he had falsely used the title Doctor of Law.
Kalvoda, who will also quit parliament, is the head of the coalition government's smallest party - the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA).

Inconclusive elections at the end of May deprived the centre-right government of its majority in Parliament adding a note of uncertainty to the political situation in one of post communist eastern Europe's most stable countries.
